page.layout: One column of running text, with a Greek line at the top under the running head. The page ends the previous sermon (AMEN), then opens Concio XV: a heading, a Scripture reference, and an italic passage beginning with a woodcut initial. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: [illegible, ~40 letters]
Sicut enim accensa pyra, & qui propè habi-
tant, periculi sunt participes, igne omnia de-
pascente: eodem modo & hic adolescentis in
temperantia, non solùm patrem, sed & omnes
ciues perdit. Ita vnius Paridis adulterium
toti Troiae exitio fuit. Non enim ij solùm di-
gni sunt morte, qui iniusta faciunt: verùm
etiá qui assentiuntur ijs, qui ea faciunt, Rom.2.
Adde quòd Sichemitae (quorum passio iniu-
sta fuit, etsi actio filiorum Iacob iniusta erat)
non solùm propter vitium, quo familiam san-
ctam Iacobæam polluerunt, sed etiam pro-
pter hypocrisim, perditi sunt. A-
usi sunt sacris sancti populi, suscepta circum-
cisione, cùm interim neque Dei Israelitarum
gloriam, neque populi electi commoditates,
sed suas spectarent. Ab eiusmodi horrenda
simulatione, necnon ab omni fornicatione
custodiat nos sancta veritas, Christus Iesus.
A M E N.
CONCIO XV.
Genes. 39.

l.i: atque pulchræ aspectu. Factumque est post hæc

main_text.l: hac

page.notes: The first line under the running head is printed in Greek; the letters are too faint to read reliably, so it is marked illegible. The opening Latin line is a continuation from the previous sermon, so its paragraph is marked cont="true". The woodcut initial D is read as the first letter of "Dimisit". Long s (printed as f) is normalised to s throughout, e.g. "ausi", "suscepta", "Israelitarum", "Genes.". The last line "hac" is the printed word-end of the verse, shown as an <l>.
